title: Transient shadow pool: handoff-driven compacting & reduced pin churn for paged KV cache
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces a transient shadow pool with lock-light handoff to reduce pin/unpin churn and improve reuse; reclaim/compact path added to reduce fragmentation under mixed workloads.
description:
Motivation: under mixed latency and bursty workloads the paged KV cache showed high pin churn and repeated allocation/eviction thrashing. This PR introduces a transient 'shadow pool' that holds recently freed blocks for a short handoff window, plus a compacting handoff path that coalesces small free fragments to reduce allocator fragmentation. The change also adjusts allocator scheduling heuristics to prefer locality-aligned reuse and adds light kernel hints to avoid expensive scheduler wakeups during hot-path reuse.

What this PR does: - Adds a transient shadow pool that accepts unpinned blocks for a configurable grace period before they become globally reclaimable. Shadow pool entries can be handed off directly to new allocators with a lock-light queue to avoid full freelist ops. - Implements a compacting handoff routine: when a shadow entry is larger than a threshold and adjacent free segments exist, we coalesce them before exposing back to the global pool. Compaction is opportunistic and bounded by a CPU budget to avoid SLO impact. - Introduces a pin-handoff fastpath that lets the serving runtime transfer ownership of a block to a new request without a full unpin/pin cycle where safe, reducing atomic ops on high-contention pages. - Adds allocator scheduling tweaks: favor same-CPU locality bins for repeated prefixes, and a hysteresis timer to avoid oscillation between pools. - Adds unit and integration tests covering handoff races, compaction budget exhaustion, and metrics. - Documented new knobs in docs/ops/kv-cache.md and added a short explainer in CHANGELOG.

Compatibility and safety: The handoff fastpath is gated behind a runtime flag (kv.shadow_handoff_enabled=false by default) and a strict verification step that rejects handoff when there are any outstanding long-lived transactions. Compaction runs with a bounded work budget and will fallback to the previous fast free path if it cannot complete within the budget. No on-disk format changes.

Performance summary (local bench): - 95th percentile token latency improved by 12% under mixed read/write workloads with small working set churn. - End-to-end throughput improved by ~8% under high-concurrency synthetic workloads due to reduced allocator CAS contention. - Memory fragmentation metric (measured as external fragmentation ratio) decreased ~15% in long-running steady-state runs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and benchmarks attached (ENG-7721) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests (kv-cache stress harness) - [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag - [x] Docs updated - [x] Smoke-tested on canary cluster

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to race handling in handoff_queue.{cc,h} and to the compaction budget enforcement in compactor.{cc}. The patch that touches scheduler hints is deliberately small; we're conservative there to avoid regressions.

References: ENG-7721 (design), ENG-7815 (bench harness), SUP-234 (customer incident that motivated change)
